analysis: Examined two provider-side changes. (1) DistributedResidentExecution.swift:82-89: the supportsLogprobs derivation moved from an inline GLM/Qwen-tensor check to ClusterModelFeaturePolicy.capturesLogprobs(capability, mode:). The call site is the only visible change. The refusal path at line 372 (logprobCaptureUnsupported) still gates p.topLogprobs > 0 on supportsLogprobs, and all other request validation (vocab, context, media, sampling bounds) is unchanged. The new policy function's body is not in the supplied evidence, so whether it is fail-closed for unknown adapters, as the comment claims, is unverified. A logprobs-capability mismatch would be an availability or correctness matter, not a confidentiality one. (2) DistributedInstalledPlan.swift: tensorParallelLaneAdapters changed from a Set to a [Adapter: Int] dictionary, adding .gemma4LayerStage with the default of 1 lane. lanesRetireAlone and defaultBatchLanes now use the dictionary lookup. Gemma 4 TP default lanes stay at 1, so the default behavior is unchanged. A higher count needs a saved width or an owner environment override (batchLanes lines 286-287, bounded to 1...8). lanesRetireAlone now returns true for Gemma 4 TP when lanes is 2...8, which assumes the Gemma4 TP runtime retires a cancelled lane alone. That worker behavior is not in the supplied evidence. The comment says lanes are unqualified on a pair, which is a correctness and qualification concern in a default-off experimental cluster path, not a demonstrated regression. The adapter environment table is unchanged apart from comments. No change touches the coordinator WebSocket, attestation, key custody, encryption, or prefix-cache storage (T-041). One unreviewed assumption: Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime batch lane retirement and the ClusterModelFeaturePolicy implementation live in other files, so cross-lane isolation of KV state or prefix cache for Gemma 4 TP multi-lane remains unverified.
